subject: Clarifying Dedicated capacity definitions and SLA credit matrix
messages:
From: Alexandra Chen <alex.chen@cascadecare.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Reza Amin <reza.amin@lighthouse-legal.com>
Date: 2027-02-10T09:17:00-08:00
Subject: Questions on Dedicated capacity definitions and SLA credits

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Before we move the term sheet to legal, a few items need clarification on Redwood's side so our procurement team can map your pricing to our internal budgeting:

1) "Capacity Unit" definition: your term sheet references capacity units but it's not clear how that maps to vGPU hours vs. throughput (tokens/sec).
2) Throughput guarantees: can you provide a short table showing expected qps/throughput per capacity unit for the common model classes (Llama-2-70B, Mix-small quantized)?
3) SLA remedies: the draft mentions service credits but not a clear tiered matrix. We need explicit % credits per outage window.
4) Discounts: we asked for a 12-month commit price; can you confirm discount tiers if we commit 3 vs 6 vs 12 months?

I've attached the internal CascadeCare procurement checklist for reference (we won't attach the legal redlines yet). Reza is copied for any contract/legal questions.

Can we aim to close these on Monday so legal can prepare redlines?

— Alex
Procurement Manager, CascadeCare

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alexandra Chen <alex.chen@cascadecare.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-10T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on Dedicated capacity definitions and SLA credits

Alex — thanks, good set of questions. I pulled Priyom and Marcus into the thread to provide the technical mapping and the commercial response. Quick answers up front:

- Capacity Unit: we define a Capacity Unit (CU) as a billing construct equal to 1 reserved GPU-eq vCPU-hour of sustained allocation on our pool with prefix K (see detailed mapping below). It is NOT strictly equal to a single GPU model; we translate model types into CU consumption based on peak memory + inference kernel characteristics.
- Throughput mapping: Priyom will attach a compact table mapping models to expected tokens/sec and typical concurrent sessions per CU.
- SLA credits: we can provide a tiered matrix. Our standard is 5% credit for monthly availability between 99.0%–99.5%, 15% for 98.0%–99.0%, and 50% for <98.0% (measured at the monthly level). We can exchange that for a stronger throughput guarantee if you need.
- Discounts: standard public tier is 10% for 3mo, 18% for 6mo, 25% for 12mo commits. We have some flexibility on the 12mo for larger pool sizes (ask Marcus).

I'm attaching a short explainer and will let Priyom follow up with the throughput table. If cascade needs a credit matrix that ties credits to per-hour outage buckets (rather than monthly availability), flag that—Marcus/legal will need to confirm.

Best,
Naomi
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_CU_explainer_v1.pdf (summary, 1 page)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alexandra Chen <alex.chen@cascadecare.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-10T12:28:00-08:00
Subject: CU-to-throughput mapping (table)

Alex / Naomi — attaching the compact mapping you asked for. Below is the inline summary (numbers are conservative medians measured on our Dedicated 80GB A100 pool under mixed traffic):

Model class -> tokens/sec per CU -> concurrent typical sessions per CU (chat)
- Llama-2-70B (quant-ptq): ~120–160 tok/sec per CU -> ~8–12 concurrent short-chat sessions
- Mix-small (8-bit quant): ~420–550 tok/sec per CU -> ~25–40 concurrent short-chat sessions
- Instruction-tuned 7B: ~900–1200 tok/sec per CU -> ~60–80 concurrent sessions

Notes: throughput varies with sequence length, streaming chunk sizes, and KV cache hit rate. Our term "CU" normalizes across GPUs by applying a model-specific CU multiplier in the billing layer. See attached: cu_throughput_table.csv (3 rows).

If you want a model-by-model SLA that guarantees absolute tok/sec, we can draft that but it increases price since it constrains routing and bin-packing.

— Priyom

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alexandra Chen <alex.chen@cascadecare.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Reza Amin <reza.amin@lighthouse-legal.com>
Date: 2027-02-11T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Draft redline: capacity unit definition and SLA remedies

Alex / Reza — per Naomi's note, legal has prepared a short redline to the Dedicated section to make "Capacity Unit" explicit and to replace the vague "service credits" language with a tiered matrix and an "extraordinary outage" carve-out. High-level redline points:

1) Insert explicit CU definition: CU = one (1) reserved GPU-equivalent-hour, where equivalence is calculated using the Redwood CU conversion table (attached).
2) Add a billing clause: for models requiring >1.25x CU multiplier (e.g., >80GB models), Redwood will bill at the multiplied CU rate but offers a grace period for the first 30 days of a rollout.
3) Replace "service credits" paragraph with a table: monthly availability tiers -> credit % (monthly cap = 100% of monthly fee). Also add a per-incident limit of 25% for incidents <2 hours.
4) Add preferred remedy: mutually agreed throughput augmentation (temp burst capacity) for incidents above 8 hours before credit application.

I've attached dedicated_pricing_redline.docx with inline changes. From a commercial perspective, we can soften the per-incident cap for strategic deals. Naomi: recommend offering a one-time credit buffer for the first contract year instead of lowering the cap.

— Marcus
Legal & Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachments: dedicated_pricing_redline.docx

From: Reza Amin <reza.amin@lighthouse-legal.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alexandra Chen <alex.chen@cascadecare.com>
Date: 2027-02-12T10:33:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: redline questions (billing indexation, caps)

Marcus / Naomi — quick legal follow-ups on the redline: two points we need clarified before sharing back with our internal counsel.

1) Billing indexation: the CU equivalence table is dynamic. Is Redwood reserving the right to re-index CU multipliers annually? If so we need an explicit notice period and a cap on year-over-year increase.
2) Cap on credits: we need to understand the rationale for the 25% per-incident cap. CascadeCare's procurement prefers an uncapped per-incident remedy up to the monthly cap, or alternatively a higher per-incident limit for outages caused by capacity misprovisioning.

If you can propose concrete language for both items we'll circulate to our GC.

— Reza

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alexandra Chen <alex.chen@cascadecare.com>, Reza Amin <reza.amin@lighthouse-legal.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-14T16:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying Dedicated capacity definitions and SLA credits — proposed concessions and next steps

Alex / Reza — thanks for the detailed points. Proposed responses below and next steps so procurement/legal can proceed: 

1) Indexation: Redwood will retain the right to adjust CU multipliers annually to reflect major hardware/hypervisor changes, with written notice 90 days prior and a hard cap of +8% year-over-year on any CU multiplier increase. We'll include a carve-out for pass-through hardware cost changes beyond our control (to be discussed).

2) Per-incident cap: commercial concession — for CascadeCare we will raise the per-incident cap from 25% to 40% of the monthly fee for incidents caused by capacity oversubscription or configuration errors by Redwood. Incidents due toforce majeure or customer misconfiguration keep the standard cap. Monthly cap remains 100% of monthly fee.

3) Pricing concession: conditional on a 12-month reserved commit at the >50 CU tier, Redwood will increase the standard 12mo discount from 25% -> 30% and include a one-time onboarding credit equal to 5% of first-month fees. This is time-limited if you sign by 2027-03-01.

4) Next steps: Marcus/legal to produce a short redline with the indexation notice + cap change and attach to the term sheet. If CascadeCare accepts, we'll prepare DocuSign for signatures; HubSpot deal updated.

Marcus — please attach the redline with the two language changes. Alex/Reza — if that looks reasonable I'll have finance produce a final pricing schedule.

Best,
Naomi
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Attachments: CascadeCare_Redwood_Dedicated_Termsheet_v2.pdf, dedicated_pricing_redline.docx (updated)
